items.title: Microsoft Research発「TokenEconomizer」がコーディングエージェントのトークン代を18.4〜30.9%削減。モデルを変えずにリポジトリ経験から無駄を学習する仕組みを一次情報から整理する
items.summary:
Microsoft Research発「TokenEconomizer」がコーディングエージェントのトークン代を18.4〜30.9%削減。モデルを変えずにリポジトリ経験から無駄を学習する仕組みを一次情報から整理する

コーディングエージェントの利用が広がるにつれ、「同じリポジトリで繰り返し作業するときのトークン浪費」が実務的な課題になってきた。モデルの単価は下がりつつある一方で、エージェントは毎回ツール定義や過去の調査結果を再請求するため、連続タスクではコストが積み上がる。

これに対してMicrosoft Research、UC Berkeley、Microsoft Securityの研究チームが2026年10月に公開したのがTokenEconomizerだ。Apache-2.0ライセンスのプラグインで、エージェントのモデルやコードを一切変更せず、同じリポジトリの過去セッションから経験を蓄積し、次のセッションの無駄を削る。対応エージェントはClaude Code、Codex、GitHub Copilot CLI、Piで、opencodeやCursor Agent、Grok Build、Hermes Agent、Antigravity CLIも実験的にサポートされている。

【日本語圏での露出】
Zenn、Qiita、はてなブックマークを中心に確認したところ、TokenEconomizerに特化した詳細記事はまだ少ない。noteに個人による紹介が10月末に数件見られた程度で、技術コミュニティでの本格的な検証や比較はこれから、という状況だ。Yahoo!リアルタイム検索でも目立った議論は確認できなかった。

【背景と問題設定】
論文「TokenEconomizer: Experience-Driven Black-Box Cost Control for Coding Agents」（arXiv 2610.22732、2026年10月15日公開）は、従来のトークン効率評価が単発タスクに偏っている点を指摘する。実際の開発では同じコードベースに対して連続してタスクを振るため、環境依存の繰り返しコストが発生する。

著者らは未修正エージェントの60タスクをプロファイリングし、3種類の浪費を特定した。
1. 同じ事実の再発見：5タスク以上進んだリポジトリではツール呼び出しの30%が過去タスクの行動を繰り返す。
2. 未使用ツールの支払い：23のツール定義のうち16が一度も呼ばれないのに毎回送信される。
3. 失敗ループ：失敗する17%のタスクが全支出の32%を占める。

固定戦略（RTKの出力圧縮、Serenaのコードナビ、RepoMapのリポジトリマップ）はリポジトリによって効果が出たり出なかったりし、どのリポジトリでも安くなる単一手法は存在しなかった。

【仕組み：3つのブラックボックス制御】
TokenEconomizerはエージェントをブラックボックスとして扱い、エージェントがすでに公開している表面（セッション開始時のコンテキスト、ツール設定、イベントストリーム）だけを操作する。学習内容はローカルの~/.tokeneconomizerに保存され、独自のAPIキーは不要。プラグイン自身のモデル呼び出しもユーザーの既存ログイン経由で行われ、コストに含まれる。

1. Micro-skills（マイクロスキル注入）
リポジトリ固有の事実（先に実行すべきビルドステップ、python -m pytestのように動くコマンドの書き方、必要な環境変数など）を学習する。失敗の繰り返しと、k=3セッションごとにモデルが過去トレースをレビューして提案する事実を組み合わせる。3セッションで確認された事実はセッション開始時に注入し、後のセッションで矛盾すれば削除する。

2. Tool pruning（ツール剪定）
p=10プロンプト以上、またはm=2セッション以上で未使用のツール、またはs=5セッションで未使用のツールを、エージェントの設定経由で次セッションから除外する。shell、read、editなどのコアツールは常に残す。1コマンドで復帰可能。

3. Failure-loop intervention（ループガード）
ターン内で同じ失敗が続く場合、ルールベースで検出し、信頼度c=0.7以上のLLMジャッジが「stuck」と判断したら1回だけリダイレクトノートを挿入。それでも繰り返せば停止方法をユーザーに通知する（自らは止めない）。成功したターン数の90パーセンタイル×1.25をターン予算の目安にする。

【実験結果】
SWE-Benchの277タスク（6リポジトリ）を5つのagent-model組み合わせで、リポジトリ内のタスクを順に実行して測定した。コストにはTokenEconomizer自身のモデル呼び出しを含む。

- 平均コスト削減：18.4%〜30.9%
- 全30セル（6リポジトリ × 5組み合わせ）ですべてDefaultより安い（リポジトリ内では5〜40%減）
- Pass@1は5組み合わせ中4で向上（Opus 4.8のみ1ポイント低下）
- 具体例：Claude Code + Opus 4.8で-30.9%、Claude Code + Sonnet 5で-23.6%、Codex + GPT-5.6 Terraで-24.7%、Copilot CLI + Sonnet 5で-18.4%

Web-Benchでは16〜21%減、セキュリティ監査ベンチ（新リポジトリが多い）では6〜20%減と、タスク構造によって効果は変動する。プロジェクトページではインタラクティブなチャートと9つの注釈付き実行例が公開されている。

【実務的な影響とバランス】
同じリポジトリで日常的にエージェントを使う開発者にとって、追加のAPI費用なしで導入できる点は実用的だ。データはローカル完結で、失敗時は何もせず通常動作に戻る設計になっている。

一方で限界もある。
- 効果は学習が進むにつれて出るため、単発や新規リポジトリでは薄い。
- テストされたエージェントバージョン範囲（Claude Code 2.1.300〜2.1.310など）を超えると未検証。
- ループガードは停止を強制しないため、ユーザー側の監視は残る。
- Pass@1がわずかに下がるケースもあり、コストと成功率のトレードオフは個別に確認する必要がある。

著者らは「adaptive black-box cost control」として位置づけており、モデル内部を触らずに環境適応する方向性を示している。固定のプロンプト最適化や出力圧縮とは補完関係にあり、RTKとの組み合わせでさらに削減した報告もある。

【出典と確認方法】
- 論文：https://t.co/dCBZO3tqFh
- コード：https://t.co/eYVsSvDWFw（Apache-2.0、Python 3.10+）
- プロジェクトページ：https://t.co/eeS3LsbLY0
- インストール例（Claude Code）：
  git clone https://t.co/OlQSRjmvf6
  claude plugin marketplace add "$PWD/TokenEconomizer"
  claude plugin install tokeneconomizer@tokeneconomizer

GitHub上のスター数は公開後急速に伸び、11月上旬時点で5,000前後まで到達している。一次情報を直接確認し、自分のリポジトリでstatusコマンドを叩いてみるのが最も確実な検証だ。

items.title: on SimpleQA o4-mini scores 24% and gpt-5-thinking-mini scores 22%. the accuracy leaderboard says o4-mini wins. it's also
items.summary:
on SimpleQA o4-mini scores 24% and gpt-5-thinking-mini scores 22%. the accuracy leaderboard says o4-mini wins. it's also wrong on 75% of questions vs 26% for the newer one

that gap is most of why models make stuff up instead of saying idk

1. almost every benchmark grades right or wrong. a blank and a wrong answer both score 0, so guessing a birthday gets a 1 in 365 shot and "i don't know" gets nothing
2. the OpenAI hallucination paper checked 10 big benchmarks (GPQA, MMLU-Pro, SWE-bench, HLE...). 9 give zero credit for abstaining
3. take two models that know the same facts. one says idk when unsure, the other always guesses. the guesser scores higher on every one of those benchmarks
4. post-training chases those scores, so every model gets pushed toward the guesser
5. gpt-5-thinking-mini abstains on 52% of SimpleQA. that's where its 26% error rate comes from, and plain accuracy can't see it

the fix they propose is kinda old school. put a confidence target in the prompt. at 75%, a wrong answer costs 2 points, so guessing only pays when the model is actually 75% sure. the JEE and the old SAT already graded like this

i think this matters more than any RAG patch, since it changes what labs optimize for

items.title: Haystack 3.5 is out 🚀
items.summary:
Haystack 3.5 is out 🚀

🧭 New OpenAI Decisions API components route text and images and classify documents.

🧱 StructuredOutputHook for agents validates the final reply against a Pydantic model or JSON schema and retries if it fails.

⏳ Step budget reminders. Agents get told how many steps are left, so they finish with an answer instead of being cut off.

🎯 Multivector embeddings. A new multivector_embedding field and MaxSimRanker support ColBERT-style models.

⚠️ Heads-up: gpt-5-mini shuts down Dec 11. The new default is gpt-5.6-terra, so update any YAML pipelines that still use gpt-5-mini.

items.title: Agentic AI Raises New Questions for Financial Institutions
items.summary:
DownloadDownload

Artificial intelligence (AI) has moved beyond answering questions and generating content. Increasingly, AI systems are being designed to act. Agentic AI can pursue objectives, make decisions and take actions on a user’s behalf, potentially with limited human involvement in individual decisions. [...] Consider a customer who gives an AI agent access to a bank account with an instruction to manage the customer’s cash efficiently. The agent decides to transfer funds, convert currencies or purchase an investment.

At first sight, these may appear to be ordinary customer transactions. Agentic AI, however, exposes important distinctions between identity, authentication, authority and attribution. [...] As agentic AI becomes more capable, firms may increasingly encounter interactions in which an AI agent collects information, compares products and initiates transactions for a customer. That creates a new layer between the institution and the person or entity with whom it has established a customer relationship.

items.title: He’s using AI to screen existing compounds for therapeutic potential | University of Pittsburgh
items.summary: Developing pharmaceuticals using AI isn’t new, but it is laborious and often leads to a dead end. “If you generate a brand-new molecule, that’s actually a limitation,” Wang said. “A lot of compounds can’t be synthesized, and that is a big issue.” [...] This back and forth is the GAN’s training. Over time, the generator learns to generate fingerprints that more closely resemble those of real molecules. Researchers then search chemical databases for existing compounds with similar footprints; the AI-generated pattern leads to the discovery of real molecules that researchers can test — no need to synthesize a new molecule. [...] In a paper published Oct. 28 in the journal Science Advances, Wang outlined Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD), a novel, practical and reusable framework that takes advantage of generative AI to screen for existing compounds with potential for therapeutic development.

items.summary: Theo hướng dẫn, các giải pháp được xem xét công nhận là sáng kiến bao gồm: giải pháp kỹ thuật, giải pháp quản lý, giải pháp tác nghiệp và giải pháp ứng dụng tiến bộ kỹ thuật. Trong đó, giải pháp kỹ thuật có thể là sản phẩm, vật liệu, giống cy trồng, vật nuôi hoặc quy trình công nghệ; giải pháp quản lý là phương pháp tổ chức, điều hành công việc; giải pháp tác nghiệp là các phương pháp thực hiện nghiệp vụ chuyên môn; còn giải pháp ứng dụng tiến bộ kỹ thuật là việc áp dụng các giải pháp kỹ thuật [...] Đối với các đề tài khoa học, đề án khoa học và công trình khoa học – công nghệ, việc xét nghiệm thu thực hiện theo quy định của pháp luật về khoa học và công nghệ. Các đề tài chỉ được xem xét công nhận hiệu quả áp dụng và phạm vi ảnh hưởng khi đã được nghiệm thu đạt yêu cầu trở lên.

items.title: Định hướng thúc đẩy ngoại giao khoa học và công nghệ
items.summary:
Để phát huy hơn nữa tiềm năng này, bà Đỗ Quỳnh Hoa cho biết, Bộ Khoa học và Công nghệ cần triển khai đồng bộ một số định hướng trọng tm. Theo đó, các hội nghị, hội thảo cần gắn với những chương trình hợp tác cụ thể, như nghiên cứu chung, chuyển giao và làm chủ công nghệ, đào tạo nhn lực, trao đổi nhà khoa học và phát triển các nhóm nghiên cứu quốc tế, nhất là trong những lĩnh vực công nghệ chiến lược và Việt Nam có nhu cầu ưu tiên. items.title: Agentic AI Raises New Questions for Financial Institutions
items.summary:
DownloadDownload

Artificial intelligence (AI) has moved beyond answering questions and generating content. Increasingly, AI systems are being designed to act. Agentic AI can pursue objectives, make decisions and take actions on a user’s behalf, potentially with limited human involvement in individual decisions. [...] Consider a customer who gives an AI agent access to a bank account with an instruction to manage the customer’s cash efficiently. The agent decides to transfer funds, convert currencies or purchase an investment.

At first sight, these may appear to be ordinary customer transactions. Agentic AI, however, exposes important distinctions between identity, authentication, authority and attribution. [...] As agentic AI becomes more capable, firms may increasingly encounter interactions in which an AI agent collects information, compares products and initiates transactions for a customer. That creates a new layer between the institution and the person or entity with whom it has established a customer relationship.

items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: OpenAI employees warned about operational security lapses for years, sources say | Reuters
items.summary:
OpenAI and Anthropic have tried to ​maintain a more open research culture to both ⁠attract employees and foster creativity that can lead to breakthroughs. The AI field is rooted in academia, where machine-learning scientists have openly discussed their research.

Some OpenAI employees are increasingly worried about this approach as AI grows more capable, according to the five people. [...] When asked about employees' concerns and their view that management did not act on these issues, OpenAI spokesperson Elana Widmann ​said that OpenAI is one of the most targeted organizations in the world. As a result, the company invests heavily in its security program to protect against attacks from insiders, cybercriminals and nation-states, she said. [...] The Reuters Daily Briefing newsletter provides all the news you need to start your day. Sign up here.

These workers argued that OpenAI's controls were so lax ‌that outsiders, including foreign governments, could obtain sensitive information about the AI lab's technology with relative ease, the people said. For example, anybody at OpenAI who could access its code could see the technical details underlying many company projects.
